an10.95:1.5: ‘The cosmos is eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’
an10.95:2.3: ‘The cosmos is not eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’
an10.95:3.10: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’
an10.95:4.2: ‘The cosmos is eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’
an10.95:5.1: “Then is this right: ‘The cosmos is not eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’?” being asked,
an10.95:5.2: he says: ‘This has not been declared by me, Uttiya: The cosmos is not eternal. This is the only truth, anything else is futile.’
an10.95:6.1: “Then is this right: ‘The cosmos is finite …’ …
an10.95:6.7: ‘A realized one both still exists and no longer exists after death …’ …
an10.95:6.8: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile’ being asked this,
an10.95:6.10: ‘This has not been declared by me, Uttiya—A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death. This is the only truth, anything else is futile,’ he says.
